The tree drops model refs and removes/rebuilds its widget child; GObject **finalize**, not dispose or the runtime wrapper’s no-op `deinit`, unregisters and deinitializes the core surface.

**n43 embedded/macOS lifecycle ranges:** MacBase `183–188 UI`, `409–424 DUI`, `458–495 DUI`, `518–583 DUI`, `1231–1236 D`, `1249–1256 UI`; `macos/Sources/Features/Splits/SplitTree.swift:155–172 DUI`; MacTerm `694–755 DUI`, `846–870 DUI`; `macos/Sources/Features/QuickTerminal/QuickTerminalController.swift:286–312 DUI`; MacView `177–186 D`, `389–395 UI`, `408–438 DUI`; `macos/Sources/Ghostty/Ghostty.Surface.swift:11–45 DUI`; Emb `290–294 DUI`, `634–646 DUI`, `1859–1861 DUI`; App `220–241 DUI`; Sfc `829–879 DUI`. The callback is a request: confirmation, hiding a live Quick Terminal root, or retaining a view for undo can prevent or delay release. The core teardown happens on host free, not just because the callback returned. For an arbitrary embedder, the only verifiable end of the in-repo contract is the optional callback plus `ghostty_surface_free`.
